title: Survey Results
text:
Dataset
The project uses the collected 25-question printed questionnaire with 38 student responses.
The questionnaire covers mobile use, social media, earphones, sleep, physical activity, study/concentration, family interaction, values and life skills.

title: Survey Results
text:
Strongest findings


Q1 · Mobile use

68.4%

26/38 reported 2+ hours of mobile use.


Q3 · Social media

76.3%

29/38 reported daily social-media use.


Q7 · Earphones

71.1%

27/38 used earphones occasionally/daily.


Q9 · Before sleep

47.4%

18/38 used a phone often/every night before sleep.


Q10 · Sleep

23.7%

9/38 reported less than 6 hours of sleep.


Q11 · Activity

44.7%

17/38 reported less than 30 minutes of outdoor activity.


Q13 · Excessive use

86.8%

33/38 said excessive mobile use affects them sometimes/often/very often.


Q24 · Development

100%

All 38 selected education + values + health + skills + responsibility.


Q25 · Balance

97.4%

37/38 selected balanced technology + physical activity as the best improvement.

title: Survey Results
text:
Interpretation
The strongest pattern is not simply “technology is bad”. The survey points toward a need for balance between technology, sleep, physical activity, learning, values, family interaction and life skills.

title: Parent Awareness
text:
Parents can help children develop healthy digital routines without treating technology as completely negative.





Set clear routines and explain why limits are useful.






Meals, conversations and family activities should include real interaction.






For young children, use talking, reading, play and interaction instead of relying on a device for every difficult moment.






Support outdoor play, sports, hobbies, music, dance and other skills.

title: Parent Awareness
text:
Parent takeaway
Model the behaviour you want children to learn. A family routine that includes sleep, physical activity, conversation, study and responsible technology use is more useful than a simple “no phone” rule.

title: Healthy Habits
text:
The same core message can be taught at different levels: use technology responsibly, sleep well, move daily, study with focus and develop real-world skills.





Classes 1–5: Play outside every day.


Classes 6–8: Balance screen time with outdoor activity.


Classes 9–12: Protect time for exercise, sports or walking.






Keep screens away during bedtime and create a calm night routine.






Reduce unnecessary notifications and distractions while studying.






Encourage music, dance, art, sports, reading, creativity and practical skills.

Code

A. Update Quarto on Windows
Install the current Quarto release from the official Quarto website: https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/
Then restart RStudio.
Check:
quarto --version
quarto check

section: B. Install the R packages used by the project
text:
B. Install the R packages used by the project
In the RStudio Console:
install.packages(c("readxl", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "scales", "rsconnect"))

C. Render locally
Open the project folder in RStudio Terminal:
quarto render
You must see:
Output created: _site/index.html

section: D. Create the Posit Connect Cloud manifest
text:
D. Create the Posit Connect Cloud manifest
In the RStudio Console, while the working directory is the project root:
rsconnect::writeManifest(contentCategory = "site")
Check that the file exists:
ls -la manifest.json

E. GitHub
git add .
git commit -m "Deployable Quarto version 1"
git push origin main

F. Posit Connect Cloud
Publish the GitHub repository as a Quarto website. Keep _quarto.yml in the repository root and keep manifest.json in the same root.

G. Netlify — easiest backup
After quarto render, the _site folder is a normal static website. You can deploy the _site folder to Netlify without running R on Netlify.

Important
Do not upload _site as the source for Posit Connect Cloud if you want Posit to render the Quarto/R project. For Posit, use the source project plus manifest.json.
Do not use a Shiny deployment method for this Quarto website. It is a Quarto website, not a Shiny app.

title: Digital Well-being of School Children
text:
Project message

Technology is useful when used responsibly. The goal is balance—not complete technology avoidance.

Use the navigation above to explore the real survey results, charts, healthy habits, parent awareness, child awareness and recommendations.

This is a questionnaire-based project. The survey findings describe the responses collected and do not by themselves establish direct cause-and-effect.

title: Evidence-based Recommendations
text:
68.4% · Q126/38 reported 2+ hours of mobile use.


Recommendation: Encourage balanced daily screen habits.


47.4% · Q918/38 used a phone often/every night before sleep.


Recommendation: Promote a screen-free bedtime routine.


44.7% · Q1117/38 reported less than 30 minutes of outdoor activity.


Recommendation: Encourage daily outdoor activity, sports or exercise.


86.8% · Q1333/38 said excessive mobile use affects them sometimes/often/very often.


Recommendation: Conduct digital-well-being awareness sessions.


97.4% · Q2537/38 selected balanced technology + physical activity as the best improvement.


Recommendation: Promote balance rather than complete technology avoidance.

title: Evidence-based Recommendations
text:
🌟 Overall recommendation
Schools + parents + children can work together to build a routine that balances:
Technology + Sleep + Physical Activity + Learning + Family + Values + Life Skills

The recommendations above are linked to the collected survey findings. They are awareness recommendations, not medical diagnoses or proof of cause-and-effect.
